articles.title: Masahiro Sakurai Forced to Abandon Game Designers Award After 16 Years as He Can't Find a Successor
articles.summary: Masahiro Sakurai revealed that the Game Designers Award won’t return to the Japan Game Awards, as he has failed to find an adequate replacement to take up his mantle.
body: The Game of the Year Division of the Japan Game Awards took place yesterday, September 14, recognizing the best and brightest in Japanese game development. While numerous titles and creative minds were celebrated, one accolade is standing out from the rest — and that’s because it’s not coming back for future JGA shows.

Masahiro Sakurai, creator of Kirby and Super Smash Bros., founded the Game Designers Award in 2010. As told by the CESA’s official website, this award recognizes games based on their creativity and originality. Games that are considered for the award must incorporate “new ideas that are a clear departure from existing works” and “expand the form of game software by presenting new ways for the user to enjoy and play with the game.”

The Game Designers Award is ultimately granted to “the title that reached out to a wide range of people, including those who don't usually play games actively, and that made the memorable achievement of the year, will be selected as the award-winning title.”
points: Masahiro Sakurai revealed that the Game Designers Award won’t return to the Japan Game Awards, as he has failed to find an adequate replacement to take up his mantle.

articles.title: Marvel's Wolverine Lets You Have Full Control Over Slow-Motion Options for Cinematic Gameplay
articles.summary: Marvel's Wolverine has an option that lets you control the speed of the game, allowing for hyper-cinematic slow-motion action. Insomniac Games has created an expansive accessibility menu for Marvel's Wolverine, and in it, there's an option to control game speed.
body: It's very Zack Snyder-y, as the ex-DC director is well-known for his slow-motion action shots that indulge in violence. Insomniac's last superhero game, Marvel's Spider-Man 2, also included this option. It allowed fans to capture beautiful web-swinging gameplay where time can briefly slow to highlight a graceful animation or a gorgeous shot. It's certainly a great way for creators to have full control over their gameplay for unique footage.
Marvel's Wolverine is officially out now after an extensive five-year wait. IGN gave the game a 6/10 in its review, noting that the game has strong bones, but lacks enough variety to sustain itself.

"Marvel's Wolverine's slick and satisfying combat wears thin well before its conclusion, so much so that even its strong character work can't quite save it from being anything more than okay," we said.

Insomniac Games has noted that it is listening to feedback from players in an effort to keep refining the experience and making it better after launch. Wolverine actor Liam McIntyre has managed to shrug off some of the harsh comments thrown at the game, stating that he's experienced backlash before and is proud of the game that the team made.
points: Marvel's Wolverine has an option that lets you control the speed of the game, allowing for hyper-cinematic slow-motion action.
Insomniac Games has created an expansive accessibility menu for Marvel's Wolverine, and in it, there's an option to control game speed.
Insomniac's last superhero game, Marvel's Spider-Man 2, also included this option.
It's certainly a great way for creators to have full control over their gameplay for unique footage.

articles.title: Microsoft Reacts To Xbox Game Pass Rumor That Could Change The Service In A Big Way
articles.summary: Microsoft has released a statement in response to a new rumor that claims the company is considering a massive shakeup to Xbox Game Pass in 2027 that would include numerous significant changes.
body: ResetEra user Slayven, who has accurately reported on unannounced Xbox news before, said the changes could include the bifurcation of Game Pass into two tiers: one with ads and one without. The tier with ads would be $13/month, while Game Pass without ads would cost $20/month, according to the report.

That's $3/month less than Game Pass Ultimate currently, and the price cut is reportedly reflective of another big change: Microsoft is reportedly removing day-one new releases from Game Pass starting in the February-April window of 2027. The rumor also stated that cloud-streaming access is being taken out of Game Pass, but people can pay for a $6 add-on that gets you 25 hours. Additionally, the report said a Family Plan will be available for an extra $6/month.

Beyond all of this, the report claimed there will be a tier of Game Pass that costs $15/month, and for that, people will get access to select titles in the Game Pass library, along with online multiplayer. Finally, it was reported that Microsoft will also offer a $11/month membership that provides access to online multiplayer alone.
points: Microsoft has released a statement in response to a new rumor that claims the company is considering a massive shakeup to Xbox Game Pass in 2027 that would include numerous significant changes.

articles.title: James Pond Legacy Situation Is More Than Meets The AI
articles.summary: Last month, System 3 Software released a trailer for James Pond Legacy, a four-game collection for Nintendo Switch 2. But the gameplay footage was largely overshadowed by accusations its developer used generative AI to create the game's promotional artwork and cover.
body: If you go back and watch that trailer, it's not difficult to see why viewers pointed out the AI-like quality of the 3D characters adorning the game's box art and other promotional material. When System 3 responded to the accusations with the assertion that "no generative AI was used in the creation of the artwork," referring specifically to the Bovine Bomber character, this was based on the information it was given at the time by Antstream, the studio that handled the collection's actual development.

"That was the statement that we were given at the time by Antstream," System 3 CEO Mark Cale told GameSpot during a call. "We weren't involved in the process. They supplied all of the artwork and they supplied, in the process, the [work-in-progress] illustration. All of that was given to us."
Cale later provided GameSpot with the statement it received back in December from Antstream, well before the trailer was made public.
points: Last month, System 3 Software released a trailer for James Pond Legacy, a four-game collection for Nintendo Switch 2.
But the gameplay footage was largely overshadowed by accusations its developer used generative AI to create the game's promotional artwork and cover.

articles.title: The Last Of Us Season 3 Is Probably The Final Season, HBO Says Yet Again
articles.summary: HBO boss Casey Bloys has once again said that the upcoming third season of The Last of Us is expected to be its last. He told Deadline that Season 3 is coming in 2027, though did not confirm when in the year.
body: In January this year, Bloys was asked if Season 3 is going to be the last, and he said, "It certainly seems that way." However, at the time, Bloys admitted that a decision like that would come down to Mazin.
Before this, Mazin said that Season 4 was essential to bring the show to a conclusion. However, Bloys has indicated that the show may wrap up its run with Season 3, which could be a longer season.
“Craig is still working it out whether it will be two more seasons or one more long season. It hasn’t been decided yet, and I’m following Craig’s lead on that,” Bloys said in 2025.

In a big shift for the series, franchise creator Naughty Dog is not involved creatively in Season 3, and Neil Druckmann dropped out as a writer/director. People have speculated about what this could mean, but Druckmann, for his part, said he left the show to focus on his work on Naughty Dog's games.

articles.title: 7 Major GTA 6 Questions the Previews Haven't Answered
articles.summary: Netflix's extended look at Grand Theft Auto 6 has come and gone, and fans the world over are sifting through all the details about the most anticipated game of 2026. Given Rockstar's unusual move of debuting the footage on Netflix, it wasn't clear what to expect from the show, but it was a pretty…
body: While there are more details to uncover in other previews in the weeks heading up to the Nov. 19 launch, there are several major questions about GTA 6 that we still have no concrete answers for. Here are several of the biggest ones.

We've seen glimpses of Jason's house and Lucia's apartment in official footage of GTA 6, and we learned from previews that players won't be able to purchase additional houses. (According to Rockstar, it wouldn't make sense for a couple on the run to be constantly expanding their real estate portfolio, which makes sense.) Still, there is a lot that could happen in terms of customization of both these spaces, especially Jason's house, which appears to be in various stages of construction during the first two trailers.

We also know that you'll be able to alter Jason and Lucia's appearance through working out, sleeping, and diet choices. It's not clear if you'll be able to take this to extremes, or whether the changes will be relatively subtle, like with Arthur Morgan in Red Dead Redemption 2.

articles.title: God of War Laufey Now Has a Lot To Prove After Wolverine’s Messy Launch
articles.summary: A full five years after its announcement, Marvel’s Wolverine is finally out on PlayStation 5. What should be a triumphant moment for Sony, though, has turned out to be an unexpected headache.
body: It’s certainly not unusual for a publisher to drop a middling game every now and then, but the timing couldn’t be worse for Sony. Aside from managing an optics crisis tied to its decision to end physical disc production in 2028, Wolverine is coming at a time when it's imperative for Sony to find its groove after years of strategic uncertainty. Expect that tension to put even more pressure on its next big first-party game, God of War Laufey.

Slated to launch on Feb. 16, 2027, God of War Laufey isn’t a very risky game on paper. It’s par for the course for the PS5 era, with Santa Monica Studio looking to deliver the kind of cinematic action-adventure game that PlayStation successfully built its brand around over the past few console generations. In any other year, it would be entering 2027 as a strong Game of the Year contender, considering God of War’s past success with critics and audiences alike.
Laufey ’s bigger challenge is a more existential one: It needs to prove that audiences still have an appetite for Sony’s brand of big budget games.

articles.title: As Skyblivion's launch approaches, the team is looking for help to get the word out
articles.summary: The gears are still grinding on Skyblivion, the massive mod that aims to recreate The Elder Scrolls 4: Oblivion in the newer, prettier technology of The Elder Scrolls 5: Skyrim Special Edition.
body: What's notable, though, is the kind of help the developers are looking for: Not to finish the mod, but to tell the world about it.

As we approach #Skyblivion's launch, we’re looking for volunteers to join our communications team! If you have experience in video production or social media, we’d love your help collaborating on everything from trailer creation to developer interviews.

"With our release getting closer, our communications team is expanding—and we need your help spreading the word!" the dev team wrote on the Skyblivion Discord. "We’re looking for volunteers with a background in video production or social media to help support projects like trailer editing, gameplay captures, and developer interviews. You'll be working alongside our communications department to get the word out!"

Nothing about the state of the mod was shared, and that remains the big question. Skyblivion was supposed to be out in 2025 but in December of that year was pushed into 2026. In April of this year, Skyblivion project lead Rebelzize admitted "there's always the chance shit hits the fan and we suffer another major setback," but added that "from what I see internally, I am pretty optimistic."

articles.title: Say Goodbye to Fallout's Best Replacement Before it Leaves Game Pass Forever
articles.summary: I love the Fallout games, but as a genuine, original, one-of-a-kind British person, I've always explored the United States-based wastelands wondering what's going down across the Atlantic.
body: Atomfall is set in the Lake District, a jaw-droppingly beautiful region of northern England, and a prime example of how British people from the south of the country are so, so wrong when they utter the oft-repeated cliché "it's grim up north."

In 1957, the Windscale fire was the worst nuclear accident the UK has ever seen. Its severity was downplayed by the British government at the time, but in reality, the radioactive materials released into the atmosphere spread across the UK and Europe. Atomfall takes this incident and rewrites history by making the disaster even worse and introducing sci-fi elements. It also moves the Windscale site much closer to the classically picturesque Lake Windermere, rather than its real location near Gosforth.
A weekly cheat sheet to what you’ll eventually love to play. No buying, no commitment — just saving for later.

articles.title: Wardogs CEO says he won't hire devs who aren't down with mandatory crunch: 'If you care about what you're making, this is the place to work'
articles.summary: Bulkhead CEO Joe Brammer is catching heat from industry colleagues for his studio's stance on crunch. In the latest episode of The Game Business Show (as covered by Game Developer ), Brammer and host Christopher Dring chatted about Bulkhead's journey as an indie studio and Wardogs' big success…
body: Brammer was upfront that crunch does happen at Bulkhead, and if you're not OK with that, you're probably not getting hired.

"A lot of people who may have an issue with crunch—rightly so, I understand that issue, we always try and avoid it, but we don’t hide that this is going to happen at some point—they often don't make it in the door. Because we want to be known for that: this is a place you come to work hard. If you care about the work you’re making and the result of what you make here, you'll feel really valued. If you don't, you will feel slave-driven," he said.

Brammer acknowledged that this is a controversial policy in game development, which has made strides to eliminate or limit mandatory crunch following years of reporting detailing the industry's labor exploitation, burnout, and the human cost of a work culture that says you only "care about what you're making," as Brammer says, if you're willing to stay late.
points: Bulkhead CEO Joe Brammer is catching heat from industry colleagues for his studio's stance on crunch.

articles.title: After riffing on Theme Hospital, Two Point Museum studio is tipping a hat to Bullfrog's classic Theme Park in its next DLC
articles.summary: Well this made me chuckle. After starting out with Two Point Hospital - a spiritual successor to developer Bullfrog Productions' classic sick-fixing sim Theme Hospital, Two Point Studios is now going even further into the past.
body: Two Point Studios actually has a direct link to Bullfrog Productions if you weren't aware: its founders, Mark Webley and Gary Carr, previously worked at the sadly long-defunct developer, and did, in fact, work on 1994's Theme Park. So there's a fun bit of symmetry going on here.

Anyway, Rides & Relics is the latest in Two Point Museum's run of largely excellent DLC expansions; those previous releases offering some neat shake-ups to the museum-running formula by introducing the likes of zoo animals, art appreciation, and even a spin on D&D-style tabletop fantasy. And, this time, the twist is theme parks and funfairs.

By sending your new Funfair Experts out to explore the new Gearbox Fairground expedition map, you'll uncover new blueprints and perks unlocking "17+" funfair-themed exhibits, including interactive displays and antique amusements (the trailer includes the likes of a pirate ship, haunted house, ferris wheel, popcorn stand, candyfloss stall, teacup ride and, um, cheese flume). It's also possible to build your own mini-coasters - adjusting height, tilt and camber - with talk of five unique coaster themes.

videos.summary: Take a look at the PS5 Features Trailer for Control Resonant, the upcoming third-person action-adventure game developed by Remedy. Players will traverse an abstract New York beyond the walls of the FBC with unprecedented features courtesy of the PlayStation 5.
points: Take a look at the PS5 Features Trailer for Control Resonant, the upcoming third-person action-adventure game developed by Remedy.
Players will traverse an abstract New York beyond the walls of the FBC with unprecedented features courtesy of the PlayStation 5.
Enjoy haptic feedback, adaptive triggers, 3D audio, and more during Dylan Faden's journey.
Control Resonant is launching on September 24 for PlayStation 5 (PS5), Xbox Series X|S, Mac, and PC (Steam and Epic Games Store).
